source_artifacts.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)

capabilities.target: Directory user profile and group memberships
User's MFA methods are removed and a new temporary access pass is issued
Chat message to the ticket requester containing the temporary access pass

inputs.source: Support ticket, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The instruction to send the temp pass to 'the person who opened the ticket' treats the ticket submitter as equivalent to the account owner, with no verification step, so any email sender (including external contractors) can receive a credential for another person's account.

Declared autonomy is A2 (approval required on sensitive actions), but only cap.mfa_reset has an approval_gate_ref. cap.send_temp_pass is also an S3 sink (egress of a restricted credential) and has no approval gate, so for that capability the design is effectively A3 (act then report), not A2.

elements.name: External ticket submitters (employees, contractors, vendors via email)
Inbound ticket content into agent context
Outbound temp-pass chat message to ticket requester
Service desk approval queue (requests and analyst decisions)

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval gate on MFA reset
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by a human outside the model, viewing raw target/requester/ticket data rather than a model-generated summary, so it does not decay with model capability. It decays with volume: about 200 requests per analyst per shift, most routine, creates approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403), and the queue gives the analyst no way to check whether the requester is actually the account owner, so a well-formed fraudulent ticket is indistinguishable from a legitimate one.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification that the ticket requester is the account owner
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced by checking the requester against directory or HR records outside the model (e.g., a callback to a phone number on file), this does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Bind temp-pass delivery to the account owner's registered contact
controls.decay_rationale: The delivery destination would come from the account owner's directory record, not from attacker-controlled ticket fields, so a more capable model cannot redirect it.

controls.name: Per-requester / per-period rate limit on MFA resets
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the IDP or orchestration layer independent of model behavior, limiting how many resets a burst of fraudulent tickets can produce.

findings.title: Untrusted ticket content drives MFA reset and temp-pass delivery to an unverified requester (helpdesk social-engineering account takeover)

attack_path.note: An untrusted ticket (which can be submitted by external contractors or vendors via email) names a target user and carries an attacker-controlled requester identity in the sender/requester field.
Agent looks up the named user's directory profile to process the MFA request.
Agent requests idp.reset_mfa for the named user; gated by ctl.analyst_approval, which cannot verify the requester is the account owner.
The temporary access pass is sent to 'the person who opened the ticket' (the ticket requester/email sender), which may be the attacker rather than the account owner.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The approval gate for idp.reset_mfa is removed, bypassed, or changed to auto-approve (e.g., under load), or autonomy for MFA resets is raised from A2 toward A3/A4.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to send the temporary access pass to 'the person who opened the ticket' rather than the verified account owner, with no identity check specified.
States that resets require analyst approval, but the approval queue display gives the analyst no way to verify the requester is the account owner.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is just the email sender address; the approval queue shows this unverified field directly to the analyst.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift, most routine, creating high-volume approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403) that reduces scrutiny of any individual request.

evidence.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)
evidence.observation: The queue surfaces the correct target account and full ticket text but has no field confirming that 'Requested by' matches the account owner, so a well-formed fraudulent ticket looks identical to a legitimate one.

recommendations.action: Require independent, out-of-band verification that the ticket requester is the account owner (e.g., a callback to the phone number on file, or confirmation through a separate verified channel) before an MFA reset is approved or executed.

Always deliver the temporary access pass to the account owner's registered contact method on file (per the directory record), never to the ticket's free-text requester field or the inbound email sender address.

Add a per-requester and per-period rate/step limit on MFA resets so a burst of fraudulent tickets cannot be processed at the same pace as routine requests, and cannot hide inside the existing ~400/shift approval volume.

Log and alert on MFA resets where the temp-pass delivery address or ticket requester does not match the target account's registered owner contact, and surface that mismatch explicitly in the approval queue UI for analyst review.

Update the agent's instructions to require explicit confirmation that the requester has been verified as the account owner before proceeding, rather than directing delivery to 'the person who opened the ticket.' This is a secondary measure only; it does not close the path on its own.

stride_coverage.rationale: The agent authenticates to the IDP with its own service identity; the spoofing risk in this design is the external ticket requester's claimed identity, assessed under el.ticket_source instead.

Artifacts do not describe email authentication (SPF/DKIM) or ticketing-system identity verification for external contractor or vendor senders, so non-repudiation of the ticket's origin cannot be assessed.
This is an inbound flow carrying ticket content into the agent; it does not carry organizational data outward, so outbound disclosure risk is assessed on el.temp_pass_flow instead.
The identified risk is misdirected delivery of a correctly issued pass to the wrong recipient, not in-transit tampering of the chat message content.
This outbound flow carries a single temporary pass per approved reset; availability risk from request volume is assessed on the agent process instead.
Artifacts do not describe integrity or access controls protecting approval-queue records from modification after an analyst decision.
Queue contents, including full ticket text and target identity, are shown only to authorized service desk analysts, an internal audience, per the artifacts.
No indication that queue throughput threatens system availability; the volume concern is reviewer attention and is captured as the agent process's denial_of_service finding.

rating.rationale: The single present finding is a complete path from an untrusted, externally-submitted ticket to an irreversible credential-issuing action (MFA reset) and an egress action (temp-pass delivery) that can send a restricted credential to an unverified requester identity. Inherent risk is critical: untrusted source to an S3 sink, with no stated step or runtime limits (autonomy modifier applies). The only mitigating control is a human approval gate on the reset step. It is structural and shows raw ticket/target data rather than a model summary, earning one tier of credit (rubric 5, step 2), but its very high daily volume (about 200 requests per analyst per shift, mostly routine) produces approval fatigue, and more fundamentally the queue never shows the analyst any check that the requester matches the account owner, so residual risk remains high rather than dropping further. If that gate is weakened, bypassed, or removed under an autonomy increase or control removal, the finding reverts to critical, which sets the forecast rating. The control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.analyst_approval.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, approval queue display, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest or IdP API configuration was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact credential_scope of the service account used for idp.reset_mfa) is inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, which lowers confidence on that field.

No information was provided on ticket-intake authentication (for example, SPF/DKIM or ticketing-system identity verification) or on logging and audit-trail details beyond the approval queue display, which limits assessment of repudiation and detection controls.
